name: tradeforge
description: Event-driven backtesting and live execution platform for trading strategies.
devDependenciesComment: `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` are here, at the root, and the root runs no tests of
its own. They are hoisted on purpose, and it took two rounds to land:
1. `@testing-library/jest-dom` 7.0.1 declares vitest as an OPTIONAL peer and ships a
`dist/vitest.mjs` that imports it at runtime. npm hoists jest-dom to the root but nests
vitest under each workspace, because `@vitest/coverage-v8` peers on an EXACT vitest
version — so the import resolved from the root, found nothing, and all 51 suites failed
2. Declaring vitest alone moved the failure one level down: the root vitest then could not
find `@vitest/coverage-v8`, still nested. A shared runner needs its plugin beside it.
Keep both in step with the workspaces. The day jest-dom stops shipping that entry point,
overridesComment: Transitive pins held ahead of what our direct dependencies ask for. Every key under
`overrides` is read by npm as a package name, so this note lives outside it.
Each entry is an advisory whose fix exists but is out of reach: npm will not raise a
transitive dependency on its own, so `npm audit fix` reports nothing to do while the
audit job keeps failing. Prefer an entry here over one in .github/audit-allowlist.json
whenever a real patch exists — an allowlist entry argues a vulnerability away, this one
closes it. Drop an entry once every dependent asks for the fixed version by itself.
js-yaml: GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj, quadratic CPU on !!omap. Reached only through
@commitlint/cli and json-schema-to-typescript, both dev-only and build-time. 4.3.1 is
the patch on the 4.x line (npm tag v4-legacy); both dependents ask for ^4.
nanoid: GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8, custom generators loop forever at size zero. Reached only
through vite -> postcss, dev-only and build-time. 3.3.18 is the patch on the 3.x line
(npm tag legacy), same bin and engines as 3.3.16.
